object_description: perimeter-filling volume with staggered heights over a two-storey base carrying a rooftop pitch
design_condition: the building occupies practically the entire perimeter and fits the large-scale quarter, distinguishing itself as a public building through staggered volumes, with the pitch and break area lifted onto roof terraces

positive: The staggering of buildings works as an effective differentiation of scale that distinguishes it as a public building
Different storey numbers, storey heights and outdoor spaces form an interesting structure
The large two-storey loggia forms the urban entrance to the school
Thanks to its position at the footbridge the rooftop pitch still has the desired public effect
The materiality of concrete and brickwork promises a strong, atmospherically convincing building
The main entrance and the separate entrances for kindergarten and sports hall are gathered on the large loggia
The sports hall and communal area become a completely autonomous public space usable outside school hours
Perfect and very determined year clusters develop over three storeys with access to the two roof terraces
The classrooms are free of disturbing views from the terraces
The skeleton construction allows basic flexibility and adaptability
The construction with repetitive concrete frames, timber-concrete composite ceilings and prefabricated facade elements is interesting
The photovoltaic system on the roof is sufficient and retention is possible
The clear and uncluttered concept is implemented seriously and promises a school that is easy to use
negative: In its depicted joint the materialisation appears more like a thin dress
The height offset of the footbridge is viewed critically in functional terms
The rooftop pitch is too small and its playability is restricted by the footbridge access
The playground as second open space on the building is not publicly accessible to the neighbourhood
The clearly structured building has a relatively large volume with large roofs and walls
The loggia is the only public outdoor space at ground level and the break area is not accessible independently of the school
The overly private spiral staircase access devalues the footbridge in its important connecting function
